slot.brief: Ask to identify the functional group or general rule from nomenclature for a simple branched compound (e.g., naming with lowest locants)

stem: The correct IUPAC name of the compound $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$ is:

verdicts.working: Choose the five-carbon chain containing the triple bond and number from the alkyne end: pent-1-yne, with a methyl group at C4.

working:
Longest chain containing the triple bond has 5 carbon atoms: pent-yne.
Number from the end nearer the triple bond: triple-bond locant $1$; methyl locant $4$.
Name: 4-methylpent-1-yne.

Independent check: Choose the five-carbon chain containing the triple bond and number from the alkyne end: pent-1-yne, with a methyl group at C4.
solution:
The longest chain containing the triple bond has five carbons. Number from the end nearer the triple bond to give it the lowest locant:
$$\text{CH}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$
The triple bond is at C1 and the methyl group at C4, so the name is 4-methylpent-1-yne.
